candidate.hypothesis: Roofline-style stage boundaries can identify cache, model enqueue, sampling enqueue, lazy evaluation, and result-delivery ownership without adding an explicit MLX evaluation barrier.
candidate.name: bounded-decode-stage-observer
candidate.rollback: Set engine.decode_stage_observer_max_events=0; zero bypasses timing calls, event construction, and observer accumulation.
candidate.scope: Aster ModelRunner single and batch decode paths only; benchmark process opt-in.

execution.pairing: Each repetition uses one observer-off and one observer-on fresh process with identical public source, model, tokenizer, input manifest, execution contract, and engine order metadata.
execution.state_assignment: observer-off and observer-on are paired within each repetition; no state timing is interpreted unless all no-op gates pass.

stage_attribution.boundary: decode driver including cache preparation, model enqueue, sampler graph enqueue, lazy evaluation/materialization window, and result delivery.
stage_attribution.caveat: The evaluation window includes deferred MLX work released by existing result materialization; it is not a private kernel attribution.
stage_attribution.method: Use the LLMVisor piecewise attribution idea as a measurement layout, while retaining MLX lazy execution and the existing sampler/materialization barrier.

summary.interpretation: Raw performance and stage measurements are valid for this fresh-source matrix. Stage shares are diagnostic only because the observer fails the no-op screen; they do not authorize a production optimization.
